Muhammad Ohiullah, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
lsrat Jahan, DAG ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Pacific Ocean Lines  ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh & others   ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Shahidul Karim J : By this Rule the respondents were called upon to show cause as to why the order as contained in নথি নং ৫ম (১)১২/কাস/আপীল/চট্ট 2030/2544 dated 15-7-2010 (Annexure- G) issued by respondent No. 2 on behalf of respondent No. 1 directing the petitioner to deposit 50% of the penalty amount in cash in the appeal pending before respondent No.' I arising out of Adjudication Order No. 15 dated 4-1-2010 passed by Respondent: No. 5 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the aforesaid appeal should be not heard and disposed of accepting the bank Guarantee already furnished by the petitioner for the entire penalty amount before respondent No.1 and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant, for the purpose of disposal of the Rule are, In brief, that the petitioner is a proprietorship firm and is engaged in the business of a shipping agent and do all kinds of acts, things and deeds relating thereto. The petitioner is also the shipping agent of the vessel MT Pujawatt' which arrived at Chittagong port on 21-5-2008 with a cargo of 11,500 metric tons of Crude Degummed Soyabean Oil (CDSO). Upon arrival of the said vessel at the outer anchorage of the Chittagong port, an ullage survey was carried out by a qualified Government surveyor in presence of all including the customs officer on duty on board the vessel and a quantity of 11,478.119 metric tons of CDSO was ascertained on board the vessel prior to discharging of the cargo therefrom. Thereupon, the entire quantity of the said Crude Degummed Soyabean Oil (CDSO) was discharged by the vessel in full in to the shore tanks at the port of Chittagong and there remained no cargo of CDSO on board the vessel. ' On completion of the discharge of the entire quantity of CDSO into the shore tanks, the tanks of the vessel were inspected and checked by all the parties concerned including the customs officer on duty on board the vessel and a Dry. Tank Certificate certifying as to the dryness and emptiness of the tanks was issued. Subsequently, the Respondent No.4 issued a letter of call dated 19-11-2008. to the petitioner relating to a short- landed quantity of 31.080 metric tons of CDSO from the vessel when the petitioner submitted its explanations by giving its comments on the alleged shortage of CDSO. Thereafter; the Adjudication Officer i.e. the Respondent No.4 however most illegally and without considering the explanations of the petitioner arbitrarily imposed a penalty of Taka 8,15,667 for the alleged short-landed quantity of 31.080 metric tons of CDSO. Against the aforesaid order the petitioner preferred an appeal under section 193 of the Customs Act, 1969 together with an application praying for dispensation of the deposit or the. penalty amount before the hearing of the appeal. The Respondent No.3 however vide its letters dated 20-6-2010 and 6-7-2010 called upon the petitioner to deposit the entire amount of Taka 8,15,667 within 10 days. But due to financial hardship, the petitioner submitted a Bank Guarantee covering the entire penalty amount in favour of the Respondent No. 1. Thereafter, the Respondent No.2 vide letter dated 15-7-2010 most illegally and arbitrarily directed the petitioner to deposit the penalty amount by way of 50% in cash and 50% in Rank Guarantee, failing which the appeal would be rejected.

3. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the above action of the respondents, the petitioner finding no other efficacious remedy moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

4. Mr Muhammad Ohidullah, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that since financial hardship was asserted and a bank guarantee was submitted by the petitioner covering the entire penalty amount, the respondents ought to have accepted the same in exercise of the discretion vested upon them by the 2nd proviso of section 194 of the Customs Act, 1969. But inspite of doing that, the respondents No.2 most illegally and arbitrarily directed the petitioner to deposit the penalty amount by way of 50% in cash and 50% in Bank guarantee and made the same a condition precedent of acceptance of the appeal ignoring the fact that the petitioner is a mere agent of the vessel in question who does not hold any fund from the principal as well as the very fact of his financial hardship" Referring to the case of Rainbow shipping Lines vs Collector of Cus toms, 53 DLR 408,. Seabon Shipping Ltd. vs Commissioner of Customs, 6 BLC 516, Sentrans Maritime (Bd) limited vs The Commissioner of Customs, 6 MLR 2001,249 and Ocean Trade Ltd. vs The Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT, 11 BLT 2003, 438 Mr Ohidullah lastly submits that in a number cases similar issue of filing appeal before the commissioner of customs on furnishing. 100% Bank. Guarantee of the penalty amount was raised and settled by this Court and since the petitioner standing -on the same footing, his case can be dealt with in the like manner.

5. Ms Israt Jahan, learned Deputy Attorney- General opposes the Rule.

6. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner as well as the learned Deputy Attorney-General and perused the writ petitioner along with the annexures and also considered the facts and circumstances of the case.

7. Admittedly, the petitioner firm is the shipping agent of the vessel in question, namely, MT PUJAWATT which was penalized by the custom authority for alleged of short-landed of 31,080 metric tons of CDSO. Materials on record clearly show that the petitioner preferred an appeal against the above adjudication order to the Respondent No. 1 along with an application praying for dispensation of the deposit of the penalty amount before the hearing of the appeal. Subsequently, the petitioner furnished' a bank guarantee for Taka 8,15,667 issued by Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited, Dhaka being No. GTEDAK. 105434 dated 31-5- 2010 covering the entire penalty amount in favour of respondent No. 1 together with an application for acceptance of the same. It Appears further from annexure-C that in Para 11 of the Memo of Appeal the petitioner disclosed that as the agent of the ship in question they did not hold any fund from its foreign principal as well as they had been subjected to manifold miseries for which making deposit of entire penalty amount in cash is not possible on its part. But in-spite of that, as it appears for annexure-G, the respondent No.2 directed the petitioner to deposit 50% of the penalty amount in cash and 50% by way of Bank Guarantee within next 10 (ten) days from 15-7- 2010, failing which the appeal preferred by the petitioner would be rejected considering the same to be incomplete. Annexure-G does not show any consideration of any hardship as to deposit. of 50% penalty in cash, instead without exercising the discretion the respondent No.2 has arbitrarily issued the said annexure which is not sustainable in law.

8. In this context it would be profitable for refer to section 194 of the Customs Act which reads as under:

"194. Deposit, Pending appeal, of duty demanded or penalty levied-(1) Any person desirous of appealing under section 193 or section 196A against any decision or order relating to any duty demanded in respect of goods which have ceased to be under the control of customs authorities or to any penalty levied under this Act shall, at the time of filing his appeal or if he is so permitted by. the appellate authority at any later stage before the consideration of the appeal, deposit with the appropriate officer fifty percent of the duty demanded or fifty percent of the penalty imposed, or both, as the case may be:

Provided that such person may, instead of depositing the amount of the penalty as aforesaid deposit only fifty percent thereof and furnish a guarantee from a scheduled bank for the due payment of the balance:

Provided further that where, in any particular case, the appellate authority is of the opinion that the deposit of duty demanded or penalty imposed will cause undue hardship to the appellant, it may dispense with such deposit, either unconditionally or subject to such conditions as it may deem fit to impose. (2) ……………	"

<u>9. From a plain reading of the aforesaid provisions of law it appears manifestly that 2nd proviso of section 194 of the said Act has given discretion upon the appellate authority to dispense with the deposit of the penalty amount either conditionally or unconditionally on the ground of undue hardship of the appellant. Since financial hardship was asserted on behalf of the petitioner claiming that they did not hold any fund from its principal and as 100% Bank guarantee was submitted for the entire penalty amount, the respondent No. 2 could have exercised his discretion by accepting the said Bank guarantee. Refusing to exercise such discretion by the respondent No.2 has 'rendered his action unjust and not sustainable in law. It reveals further from the materials on record that the matter in issue in the instant case has already been settled by this Division on a number of occasions.</u>

10. In the case of Rainbow Shipping Lines vs Collector of Customs, 53 DLR 408, it was observed as follows:

"It appears from annexures that the petitioner has stated the hardship in paying the 50% penalty in cash and also furnished Bank guarantee for the entire amount being No. GT02/2000/0014 dated 25-1-2000 covering the entire penalty amount of Taka 24,67,496,000. from ANZ Grind lays Bank Limited. The said' impugned order does not show any consideration of any hardship as to . deposit of 50% penalty; instead without exercising the discretion the respondent No: 1 has arbitrarily issued the, impugned order which is not sustainable in law. In view of the fact that legal complication would 'arise, in transmitting 50% of the penalty in foreign exchange until disposal of the appeal finally and there would be 'obvious restriction by the Bangladesh Bank pending the final decision in appeal and the time that would be consumed in transmitting the amount for preparing in appeal and that the penalty is secured by 100% Bank guarantee from' ANZ Grindlays Bank.. Chittagong, ends of justice would be best served if the petitioner is allowed to prosecute the appeal directing acceptance of Bank guarantee for the, 100% of the penalty amount which is already on record in the Appeal. In view of the above we direct the respondent No. 1 to proceed with the hearing of the appear accepting the Bank guarantee, which is for the 100% of the penalty amount and in that view of the matter set aside that impugned order dated 1-6-2000. directing to deposit in cash as has been issued without any lawful. authority. The Rule is accordingly made absolute without any order as to.

11. Similar view was also taken in the case of Seacom Shipping Ltd vs Commissioner of Customs, 6 BLC 516 wherein it was held as under:

"The petitioner has furnished a Bank Guarantee for 100% of the penalty along with the memo of appeal before the respondent and prayed for accepting the same together with assertions in the body of the memo about undue hardship. The petitioner though in' clear terms has not made out a case of undue hardship for exercising discretion by the respondent but by furnishing Bank Guarantee for 100% of the penalty has prayed for accepting the same. The petitioner as 'well in paragraph 9 of this writ petition has asserted that the petitioner is in financial hardship: and as they do not hold the funds from their principal, the 'petitioner prayed before the respondent No. 1 along with a. bank guarantee for Taka 856,882, issued by, Standard Chartered Bank; . Dhaka, Bangladesh being No,864/CC, 9900003 dated  5-1-1999 covering the entire penalty amount in favour of the respondent No.1 and prayed for stay of the deposit of 50% of the penalty amount in cash before-hearing of the appeal.

In view of the' fact' that the petitioner represented the foreign vessel and' that there would be positive; inconvenience in transmitting foreign exchange at 50%· of deposit prior to filing, the- appeal and considering the foreign exchange "restriction ,of the Bangladesh Bank for the cash amount pending final decision in the, appeal together with the ground asserting hardship' and the assertions made in the application and that the penalty amount is' secured by a 100% Bank guarantee furnished by Standard Chartered Bank, Dhaka, ends of Justice would 'be best served if the Petitioner is allowed to prefer the appeal with l 00% Bank guarantee instead of  50.% deposit in cash.

In view of the above; the respondent No. I .is directed to admit the appeal with the . Bank guarantee for the entire amount of fine filed before .him· instead. of . 50% Bank Guarantee and 50% in cash, setting aside the . impugned order in the circumstances to have been issued without  any law authority.

In the result, this' Rule, is made absolute without any order as to costs.

12. In the case of 'Sentrdns Maritime (Bd) Limited vs The Commissioner df Customs, 6 MLR' 2001, 251 wherein it was held as follows:

In view of the fact ·that the petitioner  represented the .foreign vessel and that there - would be positive inconvenience in transmitting-foreign exchange at 50% of  deposit prior to filing the., Appeal and considering the foreign exchange restriction  of the Bangladesh Bank for the· case amount pending final decision in the appeal together with the ground. asserting hardship and the assertions made in the application and that the penalty amount is secured by a 100% Bank Guarantee furnished by Agrani Bank, Chittagong, ends - of justice would he best served if the petitioner is allowed to prefer the appeal with-l00% Bank guarantee instead of  50% deposit in cash."

13. In the case of Ocean Trade Ltd vs The Commissioner- of Customs, Excise and VAT, 11 BLT 2003, 440 this Court on the self-same issue observed as follows:

"The petitioner has taken a ground of hardship and also has furnished a bank guarantee for the full amount. The Commissioner of Customs being an appellate authority by exercising his statutory discretionary power could have accepted the appeal. In view of the facts and circumstances the impugned order is liable to be set aside and struck' down. The Commissioner of appeal is directed to admit the appeal and dispose of the same - within 3 months from date of receipt of this order upon famishing bank guarantee by the appellant for the entire amount instead of 50% bank guarantee and 50% in cash."

14. We don't find any plausible ground to deviate ourselves from the decisions arrived at by their lordships in the cited cases, rather we are in full agreement with the same since the facts and circumstances of the aforesaid cases are similar with that of the instant one in our hard.

15. In the premises aforesaid, we find substance in the Rule.

16. Accordingly, The Rule is made absolute. Respondent No.1 is directed to admit the appeal with the 100% Bank guarantee of the entire penalty amount instead of 50% Bank guarantee and 50% in cash and in that view of the matter, the impugned order dated 15-7-2010 is hereby set-aside adjudging the same to be unjust and without any lawful authority.

However, there would be no order as to costs.

End.
